Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Suneel Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Moti Lal, learned
A.G.A. for the State.

2. This is an application under Section 482 of CrPC preferred by the applicant for quashing the
entire proceeding as well as summoning order dated 21.07.2023 passed by Civil Judge (J.D.)/F.T.C.,
Rampur, in Complaint Case No. 426 of 2023, (Bitto Devi Vs. Munish and others), under section 323,
504, 506 of I.P.C., Police Station Milak, District Rampur and consequential proceeding of the case.

sentences.text:
3. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that a complaint was lodged by O.P. No.2 on 04.02.2023/ 15.02.2023 against the applicant under Sections 323, 504, 506, 427, 354, 379 IPC with an allegation that on 11.01.2023 at 06:00 in the evening when the O.P. No.2 was returning after purchasing some items, then the applicants near a agricultural field, pounced upon the O.P. No.2 with the aid of fists and legs, they assaulted and thereafter with bad intention, touched the vital Tinku And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61062403/
1 parts of O.P. No.2 and took away an amount of Rs.1950/- and a complaint was lodged before S.P.,
Rampur on 12.01.2023 followed by the complaint.

Post recording of the statements under Section 200 of CrPC of the complainant, Kalyan Singh and Sonu under Section 202 of CrPC, applicants have been summoned on 21.07.2023, under Section 323, 504, 506 IPC.
4. Questioning the summoning order, the present application has been preferred.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that no such incident which is alleged to have been committed as reflected in the complaint had ever occurred.

Submission is that even infact, an FIR was lodged by one Anita, who happens to be the wife of the applicant no.1 against the husband of O.P. No.2 under Section 376, 511, 506 IPC read with Section 3(2)(V) of the SC/ST Act and a charge sheet came to be submitted against Sonu, who happens to be the son of O.P. No.2 and thereafter he has also been convicted.

Contention is that the present complaint is nothing but a classic example of misuse of process of law and the same is a counterblast and retaliation.
6.

Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that whatever might be, what would be relevant in a complaint case while testing the summoning order would be the allegations contained in the complaint vis-a-vis the statement under Sections 200 and 202 of CrPC.
7.
I have heard the submissions so made across the Bar and perused the record carefully.
8. Apparently, a complaint stood lodged by O.P. No.2 against the applicants while pinpointing allegations which have been noted hereinabove.
Statements under Sections 200 and 202 CrPC stick to the allegations in the complaint.
Contention has also been raised with respect to the fact that it is a counterblast and a retaliatory tactics sought to be adopted as the son of the O.P. no.2 was convicted in the aforesaid offences.
This Court at this juncture is not required to adjudge the merits of the allegations, as they are subject matter of trial.
9. Accordingly, no case is made out for interference at this stage.
10. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicants submits that protection be accorded to the applicants till the discharge is decided.
11. Learned A.G.A. has no objection to the same.

12. Considering the submissions so made across the Bar, the application is rejected while directing the applicants to file the discharge application by 20.06.2025 and the court below is directed to decide the same with most expedition, preferably within 45 days.

13. Till 45 days from today, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants with respect to the summoning order dated 21.07.2023 passed by Civil Judge (J.D.)/F.T.C., Rampur, in Complaint Case No. 426 of 2023, (Bitto Devi Vs. Munish and others), under section 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C.,
Police Station Milak, District Rampur.
